# Interface language

English is the supported interface language. **Preferences → Appearance → Language** also offers a **French preview (partial translation)**. Missing translations, native engine diagnostics, Git/tool output and provider content retain their source text. The French preview covers appearance, common navigation and palette interactions; it is not a claim of complete French support. Other languages are not advertised. System currently selects English.

Language is stored under `mdiff.language.v1` in the application's origin storage. It applies on the next full app launch (or standalone page reload); changing it does not remount a review, replay a shell, replace a draft, change trust or affect a connection. Close all app windows before relaunching to keep one language across windows and native labels. The first authorized page fixes process-owned tray/notification labels until exit. OS-owned menu/dialog labels follow the OS. Corrupt/unavailable storage falls back to English; write failures are displayed. To recover, choose English and restart normally after saving.

`uiText('English source', { name: value })` uses the English source as a gettext-style key. Keep user content, paths, refs, IDs, keyboard bindings, status values and code outside translation calls. Interpolation is plain text and does not recursively interpret inserted content. Existing `message(id, source)` definitions retain their stable IDs; named IDs take precedence over source-text keys. Plurals accept all six `Intl.PluralRules` categories and require `other`. Missing entries use English plural rules; missing categories use the translated `other`. Translations with changed placeholders are rejected in favor of English. Number/plural formatter caches are bounded.

Run `make messages` after changing strings. The AST extractor reads desktop/shared source, named feature/command catalogues, and mdiff-owned native tray/notification labels without importing a shell, store, provider or DOM. The English catalogue is a translation artifact, not a runtime dependency. `make typecheck` verifies it is current. Source prose remains the reviewable fallback. Edit `translations/fr.ts` for reviewed preview entries; do not translate Git commands, executable names, shortcut key tokens or user-provided content. Dynamic helper/backend diagnostics still require deliberate migration; the extraction catalogue does not claim coverage of external errors or every assembled sentence.

Development builds expose **Pseudo-localization (development)** in the language selector. Save, then restart/reload the development build to expand templates by approximately 30% with visible delimiters. Placeholders and literal shortcut hints stay intact, and inserted paths/content do not change. Production ignores a persisted pseudo locale and falls back to English. Use this to inspect narrow windows, large interface size, compact/default density, dialogs and focus rings. It does not simulate an RTL language; RTL support is not advertised.

Absolute/relative dates use the selected interface locale and the local time zone; Git date filtering still uses local calendar-day boundaries. Shortcut matching is independent of translation. Composition and AltGraph input remain excluded; physical modifier collisions retain the existing checks. Reduced-motion preferences disable decorative transitions/animations in both desktop and standalone review UI.
